title: CBSE Class 12 Mathematics · Practice paper 2
subject: Mathematics
label: Practice paper
instr: This question paper contains 38 questions. All questions are compulsory.
This question paper is divided into five Sections - A, B, C, D and E.
In Section A, Questions no. 1 to 18 are multiple choice questions (MCQs) and Questions no. 19 and 20 are Assertion-Reason based questions of 1 mark each.
In Section B, Questions no. 21 to 25 are Very Short Answer (VSA) type questions, carrying 2 marks each.
In Section C, Questions no. 26 to 31 are Short Answer (SA) type questions, carrying 3 marks each.
In Section D, Questions no. 32 to 35 are Long Answer (LA) type questions, carrying 5 marks each.

In Section E, Questions no. 36 to 38 are case study based questions carrying 4 marks each. The first two case study questions have three sub-parts (i), (ii), (iii) of 1, 1 and 2 marks; the third has two sub-parts of 2 marks each.
Internal choices of the board paper are not included: each question has one version.
Draw neat and clean figures wherever required. Take π = 22/7 wherever required, if not stated.
Use of calculators is not allowed.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text:
Assertion (A): The function $f(x)=e^{x}$ is strictly increasing on $\mathbb{R}$.
Reason (R): If $f'(x)\gt 0$ for every $x$ in an interval, then $f$ is strictly increasing on that interval.
Select the correct option.
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.
questions.sol: $f'(x)=e^{x}\gt 0$ for all real $x$, so by the stated result $f$ is strictly increasing. Both are true and R explains A.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text:
Assertion (A): If $P(A)=0.3$, $P(B)=0.4$ and $A$, $B$ are mutually exclusive events, then $A$ and $B$ are independent.
Reason (R): Two events $A$ and $B$ are independent if and only if $P(A\cap B)=P(A)P(B)$.
Select the correct option.
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.
questions.sol: Mutually exclusive means $P(A\cap B)=0$, but $P(A)P(B)=0.12\neq 0$, so $A$ and $B$ are not independent. The Assertion is false; the Reason is true.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Express the matrix $A=\begin{bmatrix}2 & 4 & -6\\ 0 & 1 & 2\\ 8 & -2 & 3\end{bmatrix}$ as the sum of a symmetric matrix and a skew-symmetric matrix.
questions.model:
$A'=\begin{bmatrix}2 & 0 & 8\\ 4 & 1 & -2\\ -6 & 2 & 3\end{bmatrix}$
$P=\frac{1}{2}(A+A')=\begin{bmatrix}2 & 2 & 1\\ 2 & 1 & 0\\ 1 & 0 & 3\end{bmatrix}$, and $P'=P$, so $P$ is symmetric.
$Q=\frac{1}{2}(A-A')=\begin{bmatrix}0 & 2 & -7\\ -2 & 0 & 2\\ 7 & -2 & 0\end{bmatrix}$, and $Q'=-Q$, so $Q$ is skew-symmetric.
$A=P+Q=\begin{bmatrix}2 & 2 & 1\\ 2 & 1 & 0\\ 1 & 0 & 3\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}0 & 2 & -7\\ -2 & 0 & 2\\ 7 & -2 & 0\end{bmatrix}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: If $y=(1+x)^{\log x}$, $x\gt 0$, find $\frac{dy}{dx}$. Also find its value at $x=1$.
questions.model:
Taking logarithms: $\log y=\log x\cdot\log(1+x)$
Differentiating: $\frac{1}{y}\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{\log(1+x)}{x}+\frac{\log x}{1+x}$
$\frac{dy}{dx}=(1+x)^{\log x}\left[\frac{\log(1+x)}{x}+\frac{\log x}{1+x}\right]$
At $x=1$: $y=2^{0}=1$, so $\frac{dy}{dx}=1\left[\log 2+0\right]=\log 2$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Find the particular solution of the differential equation $x\frac{dy}{dx}-y=xe^{\frac{y}{x}}$, $x\gt 0$, given that $y=0$ when $x=1$.
questions.model:
$\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{y}{x}+e^{\frac{y}{x}}$, a homogeneous equation. Put $y=vx$, $\frac{dy}{dx}=v+x\frac{dv}{dx}$.
$v+x\frac{dv}{dx}=v+e^{v} \Rightarrow e^{-v}dv=\frac{dx}{x}$
Integrating: $-e^{-v}=\log x+C$, i.e. $-e^{-\frac{y}{x}}=\log x+C$
$y(1)=0$: $-1=0+C \Rightarrow C=-1$
Particular solution: $e^{-\frac{y}{x}}=1-\log x$

questions.text: Find the coordinates of the foot of the perpendicular drawn from the point $P(0, 0, -2)$ to the line $\frac{x-1}{1}=\frac{y+1}{2}=\frac{z-2}{-2}$. Also find the length of this perpendicular.
questions.model:
A general point on the line: $Q(1+\lambda, -1+2\lambda, 2-2\lambda)$
$\overrightarrow{PQ}=(1+\lambda)\hat{i}+(-1+2\lambda)\hat{j}+(4-2\lambda)\hat{k}$
$\overrightarrow{PQ}$ is perpendicular to the line: $1(1+\lambda)+2(-1+2\lambda)-2(4-2\lambda)=0 \Rightarrow 9\lambda-9=0 \Rightarrow \lambda=1$
Foot of the perpendicular: $Q(2, 1, 0)$
Length $PQ=\sqrt{(2-0)^{2}+(1-0)^{2}+(0+2)^{2}}=\sqrt{9}=3$ units

questions.text:
Solve the following linear programming problem graphically:
Minimise $Z=2x+3y$
subject to the constraints $x+y\ge 4$, $x+3y\ge 6$, $x\ge 0$, $y\ge 0$.
questions.model:
Draw $x+y=4$ (through $(4,0)$, $(0,4)$) and $x+3y=6$ (through $(6,0)$, $(0,2)$). The feasible region lies on the side away from the origin of both lines, in the first quadrant; it is unbounded.
Intersection: subtracting, $2y=2 \Rightarrow y=1, x=3$.
Corner point$Z=2x+3y$
$(6,0)$12
$(3,1)$9
$(0,4)$12
The smallest value is 9. As the region is unbounded, draw $2x+3y\lt 9$: this open half-plane has no point in common with the feasible region.
So the minimum value of $Z$ is 9 at $x=3, y=1$.

points.t: Correct graph showing the unbounded feasible region

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Let $A=\mathbb{R}-\{2\}$ and $B=\mathbb{R}-\{3\}$. Show that the function $f: A\to B$ defined by $f(x)=\frac{3x+1}{x-2}$ is one-one and onto.
questions.model:
First, $f(x) eq 3$ for any $x\in A$: if $ rac{3x+1}{x-2}=3$ then $3x+1=3x-6$, which is impossible. So $f$ maps $A$ into $B$.
One-one: Let $f(x_1)=f(x_2)$: $ rac{3x_1+1}{x_1-2}= rac{3x_2+1}{x_2-2}$
$\Rightarrow (3x_1+1)(x_2-2)=(3x_2+1)(x_1-2) \Rightarrow -6x_1+x_2=-6x_2+x_1 \Rightarrow 7x_2=7x_1 \Rightarrow x_1=x_2$. So $f$ is one-one.
Onto: Let $y\in B$ and $y= rac{3x+1}{x-2}$. Then $xy-2y=3x+1 \Rightarrow x= rac{2y+1}{y-3}$, which is a real number as $y eq 3$.
Also $x eq 2$: if $ rac{2y+1}{y-3}=2$ then $2y+1=2y-6$, impossible. So $x\in A$ and $f(x)=y$.
Every element of $B$ has a pre-image in $A$, so $f$ is onto.
Hence $f$ is one-one and onto.

points.t: Conclusion: $f$ is onto (hence one-one and onto)

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Evaluate: $\displaystyle\int_{0}^{\pi}\frac{x\sin x}{3+\cos^{2}x}\,dx$.
questions.model:
Let $I=\int_{0}^{\pi}\frac{x\sin x}{3+\cos^{2}x}dx$. Using $\int_{0}^{a}f(x)dx=\int_{0}^{a}f(a-x)dx$:
$I=\int_{0}^{\pi}\frac{(\pi-x)\sin x}{3+\cos^{2}x}dx$
Adding: $2I=\pi\int_{0}^{\pi}\frac{\sin x}{3+\cos^{2}x}dx$
Put $\cos x=t$, $-\sin x\,dx=dt$; $x=0\Rightarrow t=1$, $x=\pi\Rightarrow t=-1$:
$2I=\pi\int_{-1}^{1}\frac{dt}{3+t^{2}}=\frac{\pi}{\sqrt{3}}\left[\tan^{-1}\frac{t}{\sqrt{3}}\right]_{-1}^{1}=\frac{\pi}{\sqrt{3}}\left(\frac{\pi}{6}+\frac{\pi}{6}\right)=\frac{\pi^{2}}{3\sqrt{3}}$
$I=\frac{\pi^{2}}{6\sqrt{3}}$ (or $\frac{\sqrt{3}\pi^{2}}{18}$)

points.t: Substitution $\cos x=t$ with limits $1$ to $-1$, giving $\pi\int_{-1}^{1}\frac{dt}{3+t^{2}}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Using integration, find the area of the smaller region bounded by the circle $x^{2}+y^{2}=16$ and the line $x=2$.
questions.model:
Sketch: circle with centre $O(0,0)$, radius 4; the line $x=2$ cuts it at $(2, 2\sqrt{3})$ and $(2, -2\sqrt{3})$. The smaller region lies between $x=2$ and $x=4$ and is symmetric about the $x$-axis.
Area $=2\int_{2}^{4}\sqrt{16-x^{2}}\,dx$
$=2\left[\frac{x}{2}\sqrt{16-x^{2}}+\frac{16}{2}\sin^{-1}\frac{x}{4}\right]_{2}^{4}$
$=2\left[\left(0+8\cdot\frac{\pi}{2}\right)-\left(\sqrt{12}+8\cdot\frac{\pi}{6}\right)\right]=2\left[4\pi-2\sqrt{3}-\frac{4\pi}{3}\right]$
$=\frac{16\pi}{3}-4\sqrt{3}$ sq. units

points.t: Correct sketch with the smaller region shaded

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text:
In an inter-school quiz, the last question is given to two students, Meera and Kabir, who work on it independently. The probability that Meera answers it correctly is $\frac{1}{2}$ and the probability that Kabir answers it correctly is $\frac{1}{3}$.
Based on the given information, answer the following questions:

parts.q: (i) Find the probability that both of them answer the question correctly.
(ii) Find the probability that the question is answered correctly by at least one of them.
(iii) Given that the question is answered correctly by at least one of them, find the probability that exactly one of them answered it correctly.

questions.text:
In a laboratory, a culture of bacteria grows at a rate proportional to the number of bacteria present. If $N$ is the number of bacteria at time $t$ hours, then $\frac{dN}{dt}=kN$, where $k$ is a positive constant. At the start ($t=0$) there are 1000 bacteria, and the number doubles in 3 hours.
Based on the given information, answer the following questions:

parts.q: (i) Write the order and degree of the differential equation $\frac{dN}{dt}=kN$.
(ii) Find the general solution of the differential equation.
(iii) Find the number of bacteria after 9 hours.
